_comment: Enforces docs/ARCHITECTURE.md. These thresholds are defaults that encode past failures, not laws — see ARCHITECTURE.md 'How to read this document'. Changing one is a normal move: state what the rule was protecting against and why that is outweighed, and change the doc in the same commit. What is forbidden is loosening a number to make a red build go green.
_localeComment: Switzerland publishes in four languages; every other country will get its own plus English. A locale is not a page multiplier in the v1 sense — the same market in Italian is a full page with the same dates and address, not an empty cell in a matrix. See ARCHITECTURE.md 'Locales'.

routes._localePrefix: Every path starts with a locale. The WORDS in a path are translated — /de/markt/, /fr/marche/, /it/mercato/, /en/market/, and the country segment schweiz/suisse/svizzera — because a half-translated path reads as a bug to the person it is aimed at. The NAMES are not: a city, canton and market carry one slug in all four languages, so these patterns match the same slug under every locale. See the slug_ledger migration.

allow._comment: Market pages sit outside the geography tree, so they are matched FIRST and the place patterns exclude the section words. Without that, /de/markt/x/ matches the city pattern, which silently applies the wrong content floor and the wrong Event rule.
allow.name: market

allow._comment: Forms, legal text and saved markets. Noindex, out of the sitemap, out of the ratio. Matched before the country pattern so they get their own content floor.
allow.name: utility

allow._comment: The canton level. A type segment partitions — one URL per canton — where a facet multiplies, which is the distinction the forbid rule below is really about.
allow.name: region

forbid.name: geo x time (killed v1)
forbid.why: A fourth geography segment is what produced /de/schweiz/winterthur/samstag. Date, weekday and category are filters, not URLs. The canton segment is exempt because it names a level of the tree rather than slicing one.

forbid.name: market x date (killed v1)
forbid.why: One weekly market produced 208 URLs this way. A market has one page; its dates are rows on it.

forbid.name: non-ascii slug
forbid.why: Slugs are ASCII: buelach, not bülach. Umlauts in URLs break sharing and analytics.

urlToEntityRatio.why: v1 shipped ~8500 URLs for 157 markets. Roughly 1.2 is the target; 2.0 is the hard ceiling. Counted PER LOCALE: four languages of the same market is four full pages, not four empty cells, so the denominator is entities x locales. Changed 2026-08-31 — the old aggregate count would have blocked translation outright, which is the rule getting in the way of the product rather than protecting it.

contentFloor._comment: Minimum visible text characters in <main>, per page type. A page below its floor should not exist.

styles._comment: Guardrail 7, and the only one that reads src/ rather than dist/. It encodes the two rules at the top of src/styles/base.css. Measured before that file existed: 10 selectors were defined by more than one page and 7 had already diverged, at three pages. The site is going to fourteen more.

structuredData._eventComment: Google supports the event experience only on pages focused on a single event. A market page emits exactly one Event — the next occurrence — plus Place and BreadcrumbList. Later dates are visible content, not markup. City and region pages emit no Event at all.
